'''ba'a'''
:{ba'a} - 'I expect', {ba'a}{cu'i} - 'I experience', {ba'a}{nai} - 'I remember'
:(evidential)
:class: UI2
:Explanation: ???{ba'a} describes knowledge not yet know, {ba'a}{cu'i} - knowledge being acquired at the moment of speking, {ba'a}{nai} describes already acquired knowledge. The events marked with these interjections may happen at any time, thus {ba'a} might be related to past events, which you simply don't have information about yet..

'''bu'''
:(from noun or verb to letter pronoun)
:class: BU
:Explanation: From verbs: lujvo formed with {zei} are fine: {xy} {zei} {kantu} {bu}. From nouns: {vy.} {bu} (it denotes the letter w and thus isn't the same as {vy.}), {zo a bu}, {zoi ly.klama.ly. bu}, {lo'u klam le'u bu}. The following sequences are not grammatical: {bu bu}, {si bu}, {sa bu}, {su bu}, {zei bu}, {fa'o bu}, {zo bu}, {zoi bu}, {lo'u bu}.

'''ce'''
:links sets; along with..., and also ...
:(universal connective (non-logical))
:class: JOI

:Related words: Links nouns to create sumti of plural type. See {je}, {e}
'''ce'i'''
:% percentage symbol, hundredths
:(digit/number)
:class: PA3
'''ce'o'''
:forms ordered sequence; and then ...
:(universal connective (non-logical))
:class: JOI

:Related words: Links nouns to create sumti of ordered plural type. See {ce}, {je}, {e}
'''ce'u'''
:inside an abstraction of a verb refers to another place of that verb
:(pronoun)
:class: KOhA8
:Explanation: Definitions of verbs show which place {ce'u} refers to. If not explicitly stated then {ce'u} refers to the first place of the verb. To refer to the head of a relative clause use {ke'a}.
